rules.title: Sideways markets reward patience
rules.lesson: When price is moving sideways and implied volatility is high, short-term option buyers can lose money from time decay even if the stock does not move against them.
rules.example: If a stock stays near the same price for several days, a long call can lose value because expiration is getting closer.
rules.risk_note: Waiting for a breakout, selling premium only with defined risk, or using spreads can reduce exposure to time decay.

rules.title: Bullish views can be expressed with stock or calls
rules.lesson: Buying stock gives linear upside and downside. Buying calls gives leveraged upside but can expire worthless.
rules.example: A 5% stock rally benefits both a long stock position and a long call, but the call also depends on strike, premium, volatility, and time.
rules.risk_note: Options require direction, timing, and magnitude to be sufficiently favorable.

rules.title: Bearish trades should define risk before entry
rules.lesson: Long puts and put spreads can express downside views with defined maximum loss.
rules.example: A long put can gain if the stock falls below strike minus premium before expiration.
rules.risk_note: Short options or uncovered bearish trades can create large losses if risk is not capped.

rules.title: High implied volatility changes the trade
rules.lesson: High implied volatility makes options more expensive. Buyers need a larger move to overcome premium paid.
rules.example: A call may be directionally correct but still lose money if implied volatility drops after entry.
rules.risk_note: Compare expected move, break-even price, and position sizing before entering.
